_comment: Every authority the curriculum, the Library and the locale data are allowed to cite. Shape and rules: schemas/source.toml. Cite by `id`; scripts/curriculum-status.js refuses an id that is not here. `licence` and `use` are what make the bundle promise checkable: only `use: verbatim` material may ship inside a release, everything else is either restated in our own words with the body cited, or fetched at runtime and cached on the player's machine.
licence_note: 17 U.S.C. 105 puts works of the US FEDERAL government in the public domain. It does not cover state agencies, county boards, universities, or congressionally chartered nonprofits such as the American Red Cross, none of which waive copyright by being freely readable. Those are `use: facts`: we cite them as the authority and write the fact in our own words, which copyright does not reach (Feist v. Rural Telephone Service, 499 U.S. 340, 1991).

sources.name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services
sources.note: Principles of Epidemiology in Public Health Practice, Third Edition (archive.cdc.gov; lesson 1 section 7 last reviewed 18 May 2012; read 2026-10-03): the comparison group as the key feature of analytic epidemiology; experimental and observational studies; association, and the remark that epidemiology by itself can never prove a cause; ratios, proportions and rates; the risk ratio. www.cdc.gov refuses scripted downloads; archive.cdc.gov does not.

sources.name: Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: Toxicological profiles. The authority for what a fuel or solvent does to a person. The atsdr.cdc.gov/toxprofiledocs path was retired; the profiles live on wwwn.cdc.gov now.

sources.name: NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards
sources.publisher: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health, CDC
sources.note: Flash points, exposure limits and incompatibilities for common chemicals, in the public domain. Prefer it over any retailer or hobbyist page for fuel properties.

sources.name: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
sources.note: 29 CFR 1910.106 defines the flammable-liquid categories by flash point. Federal regulation text, so quotable, unlike the NFPA standard that parallels it. Co-publisher, with NIOSH, of Nail Gun Safety: A Guide for Construction Contractors (September 2011, OSHA 3459-8-11); see niosh.

sources.name: National Fire Protection Association
sources.note: NFPA 30 and friends are copyrighted standards, free to read online and not free to copy. Where a definition exists in both NFPA and OSHA, cite OSHA.

sources.name: United States Geological Survey
sources.note: Elevation, hydrography, geology and streamflow. The terrain under the canonical world comes from here. Topographic maps (read 2026-10-03): the FAQs What is a topographic map?, How current are US Topo maps? (a three-year production cycle) and How do I find, download, or order topographic maps? (free downloads through topoView, The National Map Download Client and the Map Locator), all undated; and the US Topo Map Symbol Guide (1:24,000, one inch represents 2,000 feet; perennial and intermittent stream symbols; contour interval always noted below the bar scale).

sources.name: NOAA Tides and Currents
sources.publisher: NOAA Center for Operational Oceanographic Products and Services
sources.note: Tidal datums, harmonic constituents and predictions by station.

sources.name: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
sources.note: Climate normals and the GHCN station record. The authority for frost dates and precipitation. Geomagnetism Frequently Asked Questions (undated, read 2026-10-03; parts of it describe the 2020 to 2025 model epoch and are out of date, so cite only its general statements): a compass points along the local horizontal field, not at a single point; declination may be considerably different a mile or two away; rare local anomalies of more than 10 degrees; models revised at least every five years.

sources.name: CAMEO Chemicals
sources.publisher: NOAA Office of Response and Restoration

sources.name: National Institutes of Health
sources.publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services

sources.name: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
sources.publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services

sources.name: USDA PLANTS Database
sources.note: Names, distribution and status for every vascular plant in the US. The public-domain backbone of the species data.

sources.name: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
Web Soil Survey
sources.note: SSURGO soil map units, by survey area. What the ground will actually grow.

sources.name: Complete Guide to Home Canning, Agriculture Information Bulletin 539
sources.note: The tested process times. Deviating from them is how botulism happens, which is why this is one of the few sources a lethal-hazard topic may rest on alone. Hosted by the National Center for Home Food Preservation since USDA NIFA stopped serving it; the work itself is USDA and public domain.

sources.name: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map
sources.note: The 2023 map was produced with the PRISM Climate Group at Oregon State University, whose gridded data carries its own terms. Cite the zone, do not redistribute the grid.

sources.name: USDA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service
Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material, FPL-GTR-282
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Forest Products Laboratory
sources.note: Species-by-species strength, stiffness, shrinkage and decay resistance. The authority for anything made of wood. FPL-GTR-282 is dated March 2021. Chapter 8, Fastenings, by Douglas R. Rammer, read 2026-10-03 from the chapter PDF (https://www.fpl.fs.usda.gov/documnts/fplgtr/fplgtr282/chapter_08_fpl_gtr282.pdf) because the whole-book URL returned a service-unavailable page that day: withdrawal and lateral loads; withdrawal as low as 25 percent after moisture cycling; penny sizes obsolete in favour of length and diameter; end grain withdrawal 50 to 75 percent of side grain; lead holes; toenailing; screw and lag screw lead holes; screws and lag screws turned, never hammered; bolt hole fit and spacing; retightening bolts in green timber during the first year. Also from chapter 8 (re-read 2026-10-03): nails of copper, silicon bronze and 300 series stainless have performed well in ACA and CCA treated wood, and 300 series stainless also in copper azole and ACQ; a joist hanger and its fastener should be the same metal type.

sources.name: United States Fish and Wildlife Service
sources.note: Federal listing status and critical habitat. What a player may not legally disturb.

sources.name: Energy Savings Hub
sources.publisher: US Department of Energy, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy
sources.note: Replaced DOE Energy Saver, which was retired: energy.gov/energysaver now redirects to the department homepage and its deep links 404. Anything citing an energysaver URL is citing a dead page and needs rechecking.

sources.name: Federal Emergency Management Agency
sources.note: Corrosion Protection for Metal Connectors and Fasteners in Coastal Areas, NFIP Technical Bulletin 8 (June 2019, read 2026-10-03): structural failures frequently at connections rather than framing members; CCA removed in 2004 and some replacement preservatives more corrosive; stainless or hot-dip galvanised fasteners for treated wood; higher retention corroding faster; fasteners and connectors of similar metals; corrosion dramatically higher near the coast; G185 or heavier galvanising; routine inspection. The bulletin also carries ASCE and ICC material used with permission: rely only on FEMA's own text.

sources.name: United States Fire Administration
sources.note: Smoke alarm care (page last reviewed 28 September 2026: test monthly, batteries yearly, replace the alarm every 10 years), heating fire safety (last reviewed 4 May 2023: chimneys and heating equipment cleaned and inspected each year by a professional) and the clothes dryer fire safety flyer (undated: clean the lint filter before and after each cycle).

sources.name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.note: NIST Handbook 133-2026 (December 2025): net weight is the commodity exclusive of wrapping materials. Weighing and Scales FAQs (updated 6 March 2026): commercial scales must meet state law, all 50 states have adopted Handbook 44, and a scale must be inspected and approved by the state before commercial use. The FAQ names "an active NTEP Certificate of Conformance as proof that it is compliant with NIST Handbook 44" as the most important aspect for a commercial scale. Technical Note 1297 (Taylor and Kuyatt, 1994), appendix D: random and systematic error. Its definitions reproduce the international vocabulary of metrology (VIM), so restate them rather than quoting.

sources.name: National Center for Home Food Preservation
sources.note: USDA-funded and its recommendations trace to USDA research, but the site itself is the university's. Where a process time appears in both, cite usda-canning-guide so the number can ship.

sources.name: American Red Cross
sources.note: Congressionally chartered under 36 U.S.C. ch. 3001, which does not make it a federal agency. Its training materials are ordinary copyright.

sources.name: World Health Organization
sources.note: Most WHO publications are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO. The non-commercial clause is incompatible with a bundle anyone may redistribute, so cite, never copy.

sources.name: Poison Control, the National Capital Poison Center
sources.note: A nonprofit, not a government body. The US helpline number 1-800-222-1222 is a fact and may be stated anywhere.

sources.name: Rutgers Water Resources Program
sources.publisher: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

sources.name: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
sources.note: A state agency, so 17 U.S.C. 105 does not apply and Washington waives nothing by statute. Cite it for the fact, write the sentence ourselves. Where a topic is not specifically about Washington, cite the role state-fish-wildlife instead.

sources.name: The state cooperative extension service
sources.note: Each state's land-grant university runs one, and its advice is the locally correct advice. Resolved per place through data/locales/<id>/locale.json.

sources.name: The state fish and wildlife agency
sources.note: Seasons, limits, protected status and what may be taken. Different agency in every state, same question everywhere.

sources.name: The state health department's marine biotoxin programme
sources.note: Whether shellfish may be taken today. This is the one authority a player must check live rather than read once, which is why it is a role carrying a live URL per place.

sources.name: The state or county noxious weed control board
A soil testing laboratory
sources.note: Usually the state extension service's lab. The point of citing it is that the answer comes from testing your own ground, not from reading.

sources.name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility
sources.note: Occurrence records: what has actually been observed at a given place. Licences vary per dataset and include non-commercial terms, so records are fetched when a player asks and cached on their machine.

sources.name: iNaturalist
sources.note: Photographs and research-grade observations. Per-observation licences vary and many are non-commercial.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap
sources.note: Roads, buildings and coastline detail. ODbL share-alike would attach to anything we shipped it inside, so it is fetched and cached instead.

sources.name: Wikipedia
sources.note: Useful as a starting point and never as the authority for a hazardous claim. Fetched, never bundled.

sources.name: NASA Technical Reports Server
sources.note: NASA-authored publications such as Reference Publication 1228 (Fastener Design Manual) are federal works and quotable. CONTRACTOR reports hosted on NTRS are not: the Materials Data Handbooks (CR-123772 for 6061, CR-123773 for 7075) carry NTRS metadata belongsToUsGov false, so they are cited under nasa-contractor-reports as facts only. Check the stiType before quoting anything from NTRS. RP-1228 (Barrett, March 1990, with an erratum of 17 June 2008) read 2026-10-03: thread friction coefficients from 0.04 to 1.10 and torque tables adjusted for them; not torquing close to yield; the helical spring lock washer flat and without locking ability once tightened; galvanic corrosion and which metal should be the larger; rivets weak in tension and not watertight without seals. Its tool-accuracy tables and Appendix A (bolthead markings) are credited to outside sources: restate those, do not quote them.

sources.name: USDA Forest Service
sources.note: Forest ecology, fire behaviour and the Missoula Technology and Development Center testing reports. If You Get Lost (https://www.fs.usda.gov/visit/know-before-you-go/if-you-get-lost, page last modified 4 December 2023, read 2026-10-03): "As soon as you realize you may be lost: stop, stay calm, stay put."; think, observe, plan; stay put unless very confident of the route; stay in place at nightfall, when injured or near exhaustion.

sources.name: MedlinePlus
sources.publisher: US National Library of Medicine, National Institutes of Health
sources.note: SPLIT LICENCE, AND THE HALF WE ACTUALLY CITE IS THE COPYRIGHTED HALF. MedlinePlus states that the A.D.A.M. Medical Encyclopedia, which is every /ency/ URL, is copyrighted and licensed only for use on MedlinePlus. All the first-aid and symptom content lives under /ency/. Public domain covers the health topic summaries, medical test pages, genetics pages, recipes, videos and illustrations carrying an NLM watermark; those may be quoted and bundled with the attribution MedlinePlus asks for. Default to restating the fact in our own words, which is what use: facts means, and never paste /ency/ prose into a shipped document. This entry read public-domain-us-gov / verbatim / bundle true until 2026-09-15, which told seven guides the opposite.

sources.name: DuPont technical guides (Kevlar, Nomex)
sources.note: The manufacturer of the aramid fibre a wick is made of, and the only party who publishes its decomposition and continuous-service temperatures. Cite the named guide, never "an SDS": an SDS with no product named is not a citation, which is what placeholder-manufacturer-sds exists to record.

sources.name: Peer-reviewed literature (cited per paper in the document)
sources.note: Individual papers are cited in full in the document that uses them. This entry exists so a topic can record that some of its claims rest on primary literature rather than on an agency, without pretending one journal is an institution.

sources.name: ENERGY STAR
sources.note: Recommended insulation R-values by climate zone, air sealing, and window performance. An EPA programme, so public domain, which matters now that DOE Energy Saver is gone. Maintenance Checklist (undated, read 2026-10-03): annual pre-season contractor check-ups, and air filters inspected, cleaned or changed monthly by the owner.

sources.name: Building America Solution Center
sources.publisher: US Department of Energy, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory
sources.note: Building-science guidance and the county-by-county climate region tables. The technical half of what Energy Saver used to cover.

sources.name: Federal Trade Commission
sources.note: 16 CFR 460, the R-value Rule, is why an insulation label may not advertise R-value per inch. Consumer advice pages (read 2026-10-03): How To Avoid a Home Improvement Scam (July 2022), How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Fake Check Scams (June 2025), Mobile Payment Apps (May 2022), and Auto Warranties and Auto Service Contracts (April 2024; a dealer may not deny warranty coverage because maintenance was done by someone else). Auto warranties exception, verbatim: "But if the warranty says that the work will be done for free, the dealer or manufacturer can make you use repair facilities it chooses"; without maintenance records "your claim might be denied". Home improvement page: "Consider only contractors who are licensed and insured", the licence number in the contract, and the three-business-day right to cancel a contract signed at home. Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising, 16 CFR 255.2 (read 2026-10-03 in the eCFR): "Consumer endorsements themselves are not competent and reliable scientific evidence"; testimonials read as typical; disclaimers such as Results not typical do not cure them; disclose the generally expected result; reviews not to be distorted.

sources.name: Consumer Product Safety Commission
sources.note: Injury data by product, and the safety standards themselves. Cite a proposed rule for its data, never as if it were in force. Also cited: Publication 5123 Portable Generator Hazards (102021), Publication 5126 Walk-Behind Power Mower Fact Sheet (052016), and Publication 254 Guide for Resale Stores and Product Resellers (012013 RV 052014: selling recalled products is unlawful, including at yard sales). Publication 254 also lists children's metal jewellery over 100 ppm lead, and children's products and painted furniture over the lead limits, as not to be sold; resellers need not test but cannot knowingly sell them. Staff report CPSC/EXHR/TR--15/001, Preliminary Evaluation of Anchoring Furniture and Televisions Without Tools (May 2015; produced by staff and not reviewed or approved by the Commission), read 2026-10-03: drywall anchors strongest in shear and weakest pulled straight out; drywall typically unable to take the 50 lb pull of the voluntary standard, so kits supply a wood screw for a stud; the 50 lb based on a 95th percentile five-year-old; no strength requirement for the wall anchor. News release 25-409 (29 July 2025): anchor TVs and furniture such as bookcases and dressers securely to the wall; the mandatory clothing storage unit stability standard in effect from September 2023. cpsc.gov refuses scripted downloads; both were read through the web reader. The release also says to keep cable cords out of reach of a TV that cannot be anchored, not to store toys and remotes where children may climb for them, and to store heavier items on lower shelves (re-read 2026-10-03).

sources.name: US Department of Housing and Urban Development
sources.note: 24 CFR 3280, the manufactured home construction standards, carries thermal numbers that are quotable because they are regulation. 24 CFR 3285.203, in the Model Manufactured Home Installation Standards, requires drainage to slope at least one half inch per foot away from the foundation for the first ten feet (read in the eCFR 2026-10-03).

sources.name: Joint Trauma System Clinical Practice Guidelines
sources.note: Trauma and burn care written for austere settings with limited evacuation, which is closer to the reader we are writing for than a hospital protocol is.

sources.name: Radiation Emergency Medical Management
sources.publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services

sources.name: Integrated Taxonomic Information System
sources.publisher: A partnership of US, Canadian and Mexican agencies, hosted by USGS
sources.note: The accepted binomial and its authority. What makes a species claim checkable rather than a common name that means three different plants in three counties.

sources.name: Fire Effects Information System
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Rocky Mountain Research Station
sources.note: Species reviews with habitat, fire ecology, wildlife use and human use, each with its own literature citations. The deepest public-domain species source there is.

sources.name: United States Naval Observatory Astronomical Applications
sources.note: Sunrise, sunset and twilight for a given point and date. The authority behind a locale daylight table.

sources.name: Canada's Drug Agency (formerly CADTH)
sources.note: Rapid evidence reviews. Not a US federal body, so cite the finding and write the sentence ourselves.

sources.name: American Burn Association
sources.note: The burn-centre referral criteria. A professional society, so ordinary copyright.

sources.name: NC State Extension
sources.note: The Extension Gardener Handbook is unusually complete on soils and plant nutrition. Copyrighted by the university: cite it, restate the fact.

sources.name: The state water resources agency
sources.note: Water rights, well permits and the exemptions. In the western United States, whether you may legally take water is a real constraint and the answer is different in every state.

sources.name: US Food and Drug Administration
sources.note: Regulates what may be sold as soap, as a drug and as a food, so it is the authority for what a label is allowed to claim as well as for what is in the bottle. The FDA Food Code page (content current as of 17 September 2026) describes the Code as a model that local, state, tribal and federal regulators use to write their own food safety rules.

sources.name: National Park Service
sources.note: Visitor safety guidance written for people who are actually outside in the conditions described, which makes it unusually practical on cold, heat, water and wildlife. Park-specific pages are often better than the general ones. Ten Essentials (https://www.nps.gov/articles/10essentials.htm, last updated 28 May 2026, read 2026-10-03): navigation as a map, compass and GPS; know how to use them before going out; bring a physical map as a back-up and an extra phone battery; tell someone where you are going and when to expect you back. The other nine essentials it lists: sun protection, extra clothing, illumination, first-aid supplies, fire, repair kit and tools, nutrition, hydration and emergency shelter.

sources.name: ASHRAE Standard 62.2, Ventilation and Acceptable Indoor Air Quality in Residential Buildings
sources.publisher: American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers
sources.note: The standard that governs how much a dwelling must be ventilated, and the one most building codes adopt by reference. Copyrighted and sold, like NFPA 30: state the requirement in our own words and never reproduce its tables. Where a federal regulation says the same thing, cite the regulation instead (HUD 24 CFR 3280 carries ventilation requirements that are quotable).

sources.name: The regional air quality agency
sources.note: Declares burn bans and publishes the local air quality. A burn ban is a legal prohibition with a date on it, so this is one of the authorities a reader must check on the day rather than read once. Different body in every region.

sources.name: Published alloy and fibre data (unresolved)
sources.note: Stands in for a real citation that was never made. Replace with nasa-contractor-reports for the 6061 and 7075 Materials Data Handbooks (CR-123772 and CR-123773, cited as facts because they are contractor reports, not federal works), a named producer data sheet such as kaiser-aluminum-technical or alleima-technical, doe for the general mechanical-property tables, fpl-wood-handbook for wood, and a named manufacturer technical guide for aramid fibre. An earlier version of this note named mil-hdbk-5, which is not an id in this registry: its link answered 200 with a publisher homepage and it was removed.

sources.name: Manufacturer safety data sheet (product unnamed)
sources.note: An SDS is only a citation once the product and manufacturer are named. Until then it points at nothing. For fuel properties, niosh-pocket-guide and cameo-chemicals say the same things and are public domain.

sources.name: US military technical and training manuals
sources.note: Works of the US government, so public domain under 17 USC 105 and quotable in the bundle. The hand-tool and shop manuals (TM 9-243 Use and Care of Hand Tools and Measuring Tools, TC 9-524 Fundamentals of Machine Tools) are the most thoroughly illustrated free instruction on these subjects that exists, written to teach a skill to somebody with no background, which is our reader exactly. Treat the equipment-specific volumes with more care: a manual written for one machine in one decade is not general guidance. FM 5-426 Carpentry (3 October 1995, approved for public release, distribution unlimited; copy at archive.org) is the source for building layout: batter boards, the 6-8-10 and diagonal methods, plumbing posts, stairs as a right triangle and the rafter table. TM 9-243 is a joint Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps manual (also Navy M6290-AJ-MAN-010, Air Force TO 32-1-101, Marine Corps TM 10209-10/1) dated 12 December 1984; the archive.org copy (use-and-care-of-hand-tools-and-measuring-tools-1983) is the Navy June 1992 reissue, NAVEDTRA 12085, with Change 1. Its chapter 20 also says to make certain no one is under a vehicle being raised, and to be aware of the capabilities of the jack, especially its load capacity. FM 3-25.26 Map Reading and Land Navigation (20 July 2001, approved for public release, distribution unlimited; archive.org MManuals copy, read 2026-10-03) is the source for map reading: marginal information, scale and bar scales, map colours, contour lines and terrain features, azimuths and the declination diagram, compass separation distances, orienting a map, terrain association, handrails, catching features and attack points. Its later editions (FM 3-25.26 of 2005, TC 3-25.26 of 15 November 2013) are not public release. Also read 2026-10-03: FM 5-426 chapter 2, Hardware (nails, screws, lag screws, bolts; the three-times nail length rule) and TM 9-243 chapters 21, 22 and 25 (hammer, screwdriver and wrench safety; torque wrenches as calibrated precision instruments for final tightening).

sources.name: State health department, wastewater and water reuse programme
sources.publisher: varies by locale, see locale.json authorities
sources.note: There is no federal greywater regulation. EPA runs research and a summary service and says plainly that states hold this, so a guide that cites only EPA for greywater has cited nobody with authority over the reader. The existing state-health-biotoxin role is scoped to marine biotoxins and cannot stand in for this.

sources.name: Local health jurisdiction
sources.publisher: varies by locale, see locale.json authorities
sources.note: The county or district health department is the body that actually permits a septic system, a well or a greywater system, and it is the one a reader has to telephone. It is also the level at which a state rule may simply not be implemented locally, which is not the same as the activity being prohibited.

sources.name: State natural resources or public lands agency
sources.publisher: varies by locale, see locale.json authorities
sources.note: Harvest rules differ per land category and the differences are not small: a national PARK and a national FOREST are different regimes, and state land is a third. Cite the category the reader is standing on.

sources.name: Tribal government
sources.publisher: varies by locale, see locale.json authorities
sources.note: Treaty-reserved rights are law and are co-managed with the state, not a courtesy and not a historical note. Where a guide touches who may take fish, shellfish or game, the tribal government whose usual and accustomed area covers the place is an authority on it. Represent what the nation itself publishes; do not characterise treaty rights from secondary sources.

sources.name: Federal Aviation Administration advisory circulars and handbooks
sources.note: AC 43.13-1B, Acceptable Methods, Techniques and Practices for Aircraft Inspection and Repair, is the most careful free writing on metal repair, fastening and corrosion that exists, because the consequence of getting it wrong is a crash. Aviation tolerances are tighter than a homestead needs, so take the method and the reasoning rather than the acceptance limits.

sources.name: Penn State Extension
sources.note: Strong on food preservation and storage. A state university, so NOT public domain: restate the fact, never the wording. Check the scope of what you take, because an extension article written about canning jars is not a general rule about food.

sources.name: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach
sources.note: Strong on grain storage, food safety and the growth conditions of spoilage organisms. A state university, so restate rather than quote.

sources.name: Washington State Department of Health
sources.note: A STATE agency, so 17 USC 105 does not cover it and nothing from it may be quoted verbatim into the bundle: restate the fact. Carries the fish consumption advisories, the shellfish biotoxin programme and the greywater rules. Check publication dates: the Puget Sound fish advisory most often cited is from 2015 and sits on a legacy URL.

sources.name: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
sources.note: The source of the Dietary Reference Intakes, so every RDA, AI, UL and EAR in this Library ultimately comes from here even when it is read off an NIH fact sheet, and NIH says so on those sheets. NOT a federal work: the National Academies are a private non-profit chartered by Congress, and their reports are copyrighted, so restate. Many reports are readable free at nap.nationalacademies.org. Cite the report and its year, because the DRI panels revise.

sources.name: University of Georgia Extension
sources.note: Strong on pruning, propagation and southern horticulture. Scope-check anything seasonal: Georgia is not the Pacific Northwest. A state university, so NOT public domain: restate the fact, never the wording.

sources.name: Utah State University Extension
sources.note: Good on seedling culture and arid-climate growing. The arid part is the scope word to watch when reading it here. A state university, so NOT public domain: restate the fact, never the wording.

sources.name: University of Illinois Extension
sources.note: Strong on field crops and vegetable culture. A state university, so NOT public domain: restate the fact, never the wording.

sources.name: Colorado State University Extension
sources.note: Strong on food preservation, and the source of blanching material already cited in this Library. Altitude is the scope word: Colorado guidance often assumes it. A state university, so NOT public domain: restate the fact, never the wording.

sources.name: University of Missouri Extension
sources.note: General horticulture and food preservation. A state university, so NOT public domain: restate the fact, never the wording.

sources.name: United States federal and military specifications
sources.publisher: US Department of Defense and General Services Administration, distributed through the DLA ASSIST database
sources.note: QQ-P-416F (cadmium plating: 450 F limit, vapour warning, Type II chromate colours), MIL-DTL-5541F (chromate conversion coatings on aluminium, unpainted coatings lose protection from 140 F), MIL-T-6736B (4130 tube minimums, 1965) and MIL-DTL-5002F (10 May 2022: no cadmium on or in contact with titanium; section 3.6.7(a) no silver or silver plating on or in contact with titanium parts and fasteners, and no silver-plated hardware, clamps, tools, fixtures or jigs in titanium fabrication or assembly; Table I note 2/ adds silver not against titanium above 350 F in service; cadmium to 450 F, zinc coatings to 500 F). Some were read through mirrors (anoplex.com, an everyspec copy); the specifications themselves are federal works, Distribution A. MIL-DTL-5002E (12 July 2011, superseded by F; read on everyspec, cited only for history: its section 3.6.12(a) limited the silver ban to titanium above 350 F / 177 C, citing silver embrittlement). Kept separate from dod-technical-manuals, which is the teaching-manual series.

sources.name: US Customs and Border Protection
sources.note: Informed compliance publication, Fiber Trade Names and Generic Terms, June 2006: the authoritative brand-to-fibre list (Dacron, Polartec, Supplex, Orlon, Kanekalon and so on). CBP itself warns the list is not exhaustive, and several brands map to more than one fibre.

sources.name: Defense Visual Information Distribution Service
sources.note: Military public-affairs news. Cited for the April 2006 Marine Corps ban on polyester and nylon athletic wear in Iraq. Check each item's credit line: most DVIDS material is a federal work, but individual items can carry third-party rights.

sources.name: Bureau of Reclamation
sources.note: Research and Development Office project 8623 (FY2015), Potentiodynamic Polarization Testing of Zinc Anodes in Natural Waters: zinc anodes passivate in some fresh waters, and Reclamation tends to use magnesium anodes. Related record: data.usbr.gov/catalog/8513 (S&T Project 22021).

sources.name: NASA contractor reports (via the NASA Technical Reports Server)
sources.note: Materials Data Handbooks: Aluminum Alloy 6061 (CR-123772, May 1972) and 7075 (CR-123773, April 1972), by Western Applied Research & Development under contract NAS8-26644 for Marshall Space Flight Center. NTRS metadata: stiType CONTRACTOR_REPORT, belongsToUsGov false, copyright determination GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED. Not federal works under 17 USC 105, so cite facts in our own words and copy no text until the redistribution terms are confirmed. NASA-authored publications (Reference Publications such as RP-1228) stay under nasa-ntrs.

sources.name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory technical reports (via DOE OSTI)
sources.publisher: Oak Ridge National Laboratory, through the DOE Office of Scientific and Technical Information
sources.note: ORNL-TM-4396 (Swindeman, Feb 1974), type 304 plate: only the abstract was read, which says the measured yield was near the 30,000 psi minimum ASTM A 240 specifies. A contractor-operated national laboratory's report is not automatically a 17 USC 105 federal work, so licence stays unknown and use facts until a specific report's status is checked.

sources.name: Health Canada
sources.note: Industry Guide to the Flammability of Textile Products (modified 2026-03-05): three flammability groups, weight and weave, raised-fibre surface flash, the blend scaffolding effect. A foreign government work under Crown copyright, so facts only.

sources.name: UK Health and Safety Executive
sources.note: Lead in construction: keep heat guns below 500 C on lead paint. A foreign government work (Crown copyright, generally under the Open Government Licence); treated as facts per the rule for non-federal government.

sources.name: California Division of Occupational Safety and Health
sources.note: N95 Mask Commonly Asked Questions (Feb 2021): N95s do not protect against gases or vapours. A state work, so facts only.

sources.name: Code of Maryland Regulations 03.03.05.03, Specifications for Kerosene (ASTM D-3699)
sources.publisher: State of Maryland (read via Cornell Legal Information Institute)
sources.note: A state regulation, not a federal work, so 17 USC 105 does not apply and it is use: facts. The readable source for ASTM D3699 figures from the older edition Maryland adopted: flash point 38 C (100 F) minimum for 1-K and 2-K, sulphur 0.04 and 0.30 percent maximum, end point 300 C.

sources.name: Portland Fire & Rescue, Fire Marshal's Office policy FIR 3.07, Fire Performance Art
sources.note: A city work, not federal, so facts only. Revised 2018-08-02, reviewed 2019-12-30, read in full 2026-09-24. Fuel list, gasoline ban, kerosene outdoors only, 1 gal maximum, no glass, age 18 (16-18 by exception), 20 ft distance, two safety personnel, snug natural-fibre or fire-resistant clothing and no synthetics for performers and spotters, spotter's wet cotton towel of at least 15x24 in or a wool or Nomex blanket or duvetyne, 2A-10BC extinguisher per spotter, 5 gal water bucket for cooling burns, aramid plus fibreglass wicks recommended, sprinklers and a 12 ft minimum ceiling for indoor venues, NFPA 160 among its references.

sources.name: Seattle Fire Department, Permit Conditions 2511, Fire Performance
sources.note: A city work, so facts only. Rev. March 2025, based on the 2021 Seattle Fire Code. No Class I liquids (gasoline, white gas) without prior approval, only Class II or higher; two 2A-40BC extinguishers; a 2.5 gal bucket of water for the flame devices; 15 ft clear area; no fire breathing; snug natural-fibre clothing for performers and spotters (the sentence is garbled in the original and is read as an outright ban on synthetics); cites NFPA 160.

sources.name: Utah State Fire Marshal, Artisan's and Performers Safety Standards (compilation)
sources.publisher: Utah Department of Public Safety, State Fire Marshal's Office
sources.note: A state work, so facts only. Describes itself as a compilation, not a code. Chapter 9 on fabrics and costumes is consistent with other sources; its fuel chapters contradict themselves, so cite those with care. Sections 18.10 to 18.12 (stop rolling once a blanket is ready; open the blanket afterwards) and chapter 8 on substance abuse. It reprints third-party text (NAFAA Rev 2.1; the Home of Poi clothing Q&A and flame test in Appendix B): cite that material to its original author.

sources.name: ASTM International standards
sources.note: Paywalled; cite figures as facts, never copy tables. D3699 Standard Specification for Kerosine (current edition D3699-25, May 2025; the public scope was read directly, the 38 C flash minimum through maryland-comar). B338, B348/B265, B210/B483, B221, A269/A213/A554, A240, A666, A513, B107, B88: specification minimum strengths, mostly read as reprinted by producers (Kaiser, Totten). B633-19 electrodeposited zinc on iron and steel (type II coloured chromate; hexavalent-free passivates defined separately as types V and VI), read from a finisher's reprint.

sources.name: SAE Aerospace Material Specifications
sources.note: AMS 4944/4945 (grade 9 CWSR titanium tube), AMS 5643 (17-4PH bar).

sources.name: British and European Standards (BS EN)
sources.note: BS EN 755-2, 6082-T6 extruded tube minimum.

sources.name: ANSI C80.3, Electrical Metallic Tubing
sources.note: EMT dimensions (1/2 in trade size 0.706 in OD x 0.042 in wall). Not read directly: the dimensions come from the North American EMT table on Wikipedia, which does not name the standard.

sources.name: International Residential Code
sources.note: IRC 2021 R305.1 minimum ceiling height (7 ft).

sources.name: ASME B1.1 Unified Inch Screw Threads
sources.note: Standard 60-degree thread form, external thread depth about 0.61 of pitch. Used only for arithmetic; paywalled and not read directly. ASME conference papers are cited under peer-reviewed-literature.

sources.name: DNV recommended practices (DNV-RP-F107, Risk Assessment of Pipeline Protection)
sources.note: Classification society standard. DNV-RP-F107 (2001) Eq. 3 gives the dent energy of a pipe under a knife-edge impact after Wierzbicki and Suh (1988); expanded, the diameter cancels and the force for a given dent depth scales with yield x wall^1.5. Used for the staff dent index from 2026-09-25.

sources.name: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics
sources.note: 84th ed. (2003) vapour pressure of the metallic elements (1 Pa temperatures: Cd 257 C, Zn 337 C) and melting points (Zn 419 C, Pb 327 C). Read as transcribed on Wikipedia's data page, which is itself cc-by-sa; cite the CRC as the authority and copy no tables.

sources.name: Metallic Materials Properties Development and Standardization (MMPDS)
sources.publisher: Battelle Memorial Institute, under FAA sponsorship
sources.note: MMPDS-04 (2008) figure on 6061-T6 strength after elevated-temperature exposure, read by eye and marked approximate wherever used. Successor to the public-domain MIL-HDBK-5, but MMPDS itself is sold and is not a federal work.

sources.note: Drawn tube minimums (ASTM B210/B483), densities, moduli, conductivities, corrosion and cold-workability ratings; 7068 brochure (strength loss at 150 C). Note the 7075 MPa column misprint documented in the research notes (alloys-final.json).

sources.name: Alleima titanium grade 9 datasheet and Safety Information Sheet
sources.note: SIS (Nov 2023): massive titanium not combustible, fines self-ignite, powder auto-ignition 250 C, melting at 1900 K, no water or CO2. sources.name: Haynes International Ti-3Al-2.5V brochure
sources.note: Grade 9 developed for seamless tubing; heat-treatment range 371-790 C; standard 3/4 in walls.

sources.note: Grade 5 annealed tube minimum (700 MPa); grade 9 thermal conductivity 7.6 W/(m K) and expansion 7.9 um/m per C.

sources.name: TIMET Titanium Design and Fabrication Handbook for Industrial Applications, and TIMETAL datasheets

sources.name: Zapp Titanium Grades 1-4 datasheet
sources.note: Last revised January 2022. CP titanium conductivity 22 W/(m K) at room temperature, melting about 1660 C, grade 2 strength at 315 C.

sources.name: Carpenter Technology alloy data sheets
sources.note: CP Ti Grade 4 data sheet (undated, accessed 2026-09-24): bar/plate minimum, hot strength, 204 C service limit, galling tendency, and a chart of CP titanium thermal conductivity for three heats, read by eye as roughly 17-23 W/(m K).

sources.name: Rolled Alloys 304/304L stainless data sheet
sources.note: Bulletin 1029, 2012: typical 304 yield 35/23/19 ksi at 70/400/800 F (21, 204, 427 C); density; modulus; melting 2550-2590 F; expansion 9.2e-6 per F.

sources.name: Sandmeyer Steel alloy 17-4PH data

sources.name: AK Steel Type 201 stainless data sheet
sources.note: 201 density, modulus, conductivity.

sources.name: ATI technical data sheets (stainless and specialty alloys)
sources.note: ATI 430 TDS (version 1, 2012-07-13: ferritic, 16-18% Cr, annealing produces no phase transformation) and the ATI 410/420/425 Mod/440A/440C TDS (version 1, 2014-02-18: hardenable martensitic, oil quench from 1,800 to 1,950 F, cutlery).

sources.name: Copper Development Association alloy data
sources.note: C12200, C26000 (annealed elongation about 54-65%), C28000 (about 45-50%) and C36000 (free-machining brass, lead 2.5-3.7 percent) properties, read 2026-09-24. The alloy pages refuse plain automated fetches; a browser user agent gets through.

sources.name: Materion safety data sheet, Copper Beryllium Wrought Alloy
sources.note: Version 09, 2025: the hazard arises when cutting, grinding, heat treating or welding.

sources.name: TW Metals Safety Data Sheet: Magnesium (AZ31B)
sources.note: MSDS 700, revised 2022-02-08: magnesium alloys ignite near their melting point; smother with approved magnesium-fire powder; no water, foam, halogenated agents or CO2, and water on burning magnesium makes hydrogen and may cause an explosion. A named replacement for placeholder-manufacturer-sds on magnesium.

sources.name: DOW CORNING C6-540 Liquid Silicone Rubber safety data sheet
sources.publisher: Dow (DuPont Silicones at time of issue)
sources.note: Issued 2018-10-18: formaldehyde vapour above 150 C in air. A named product SDS, not a generic one.

sources.name: Henkel LOCTITE technical data sheets
sources.note: Threadlocker Blue 242 TDS (revised 2024-10-05): service -54 to 149 C, release by heating to about 250 C, not for plastic parts. LB 771 Nickel Anti-Seize TDS (Jan 2015): nickel based, prevents galling especially of stainless, rated to 1,315 C.

sources.name: Cardinal Industrial Finishes technical data sheet C241-BK109
sources.note: Polyester powder coat, cure 10 minutes at 350 F (177 C) metal temperature. The site serves a self-signed certificate.

sources.name: Guide to the Safe Handling of Fluoropolymer Resins
sources.note: 5th ed.: PTFE hazardous fumes above about 330 C; ultra-fine particles at 420 C; COF2/HF around 450 C; PFIB above 475 C; polymer fume fever from contaminated tobacco.

sources.name: American Galvanizers Association technical pages
sources.note: Industry trade association, not a federal source; labelled as such in the text. In Extreme Temperatures (last updated Oct 2019, read 2026-09-24): 200 C (392 F) long-term continuous maximum for hot-dip galvanised steel, not recommended above 250 C (480 F), about 350 C for under 2 h at a time or a single excursion under 24 h; the outer zinc layer peels above the continuous figure. These are coating limits, not fume thresholds; the page says nothing about fume. Zinc melting point from its welding page. NASA RP-1228's 250 F is an aerospace plated-fastener limit, not a hot-dip figure.

sources.name: TWI Job Knowledge: Welding of titanium and its alloys, part 1 (Gene Mathers)
sources.note: UK industrial research body, not a government. Oxygen and nitrogen diffuse into titanium above about 400 C and embrittle it; weld colours from acceptable straw to unacceptable light blue, grey and white.

sources.name: Parker O-Ring Handbook ORD 5700, Section VII compatibility tables
sources.note: Fuel ratings (gasoline, kerosene, Stoddard solvent, hexane, mineral oils, paraffins) and service temperature ranges for silicone, fluorosilicone, FKM, nitrile, PU, neoprene, EPDM and butyl. Long-soak seal ratings. The URL is a third-party copy of the Parker section.

sources.name: Shin-Etsu Characteristic properties of Silicone Rubber Compounds
sources.note: April 2025 edition. Silicone swells, softens and loses strength in gasoline and other non-polar solvents, does not decompose or dissolve, and returns to its former state when the solvent is removed; continues burning once ignited. Its numeric tables extract badly, so only its prose is cited.

sources.name: Permatex technical data sheets
sources.note: Self-fusing Silicone Tape 82112, rev 02/2019: silicone gum, 200 C continuous and 260 C intermittent, full cure 24 h, clean off oil first, fuel-exposure statement, listed as non-flammable.

sources.name: Rogers Corporation ARLON self-fusing silicone tapes
sources.note: Bonds only to itself, permanently within 24 h; 180 C continuous; flame-retardant grade (FAR 25.853). Accessed 2026-09-24.

sources.name: 3M product data sheets
sources.note: Scotch Rubber Splicing Tape 23 data sheet, July 2021: self-fusing EPR backing, 90 C operating, 130 C emergency overload. The example of a non-silicone self-fusing tape.

sources.name: Permabond Engineering Adhesives technical resources
sources.note: Silicone is difficult to bond; only silicone adhesives, or a cyanoacrylate over a primer, hold well. Accessed 2026-09-24.

sources.name: Nord-Lock Group bolting technical articles

sources.name: DragonPlate carbon fibre FAQ

sources.name: Panasonic (Sanyo) lithium-ion cell safety data sheet
sources.note: SDS-IBT-00026, Aug 1 2013: keep away from heat and fire; above 100 C causes heat generation and ignition. Hosted by a retailer, but the document is the manufacturer's.

sources.name: Covestro, Makrolon: The chemical resistance
sources.note: Edition 2016-12: polycarbonate not resistant to standard petrol and diesel; aromatics crack stressed parts. Its table columns extract misaligned, so only the prose is cited.

sources.name: Viton fluoroelastomer safety data sheet
sources.note: MSDS v2.0, Sept 25 2008: HF and carbonyl fluoride decomposition products; above 315 C the surface may carry HF condensate.

sources.name: Coleman Camp Fuel Safety Data Sheet
sources.note: Version 5.1, revised 2022-04-07. Composition (light hydrotreated distillate 60-100%, pentane/isopentane/cyclohexene 5-10% each, hexane 1-5%), flash point below -18 C, vapour pressure 5.3 psi at 38 C, H225/H304/H336/H361, P243 static, P271 outdoors, do not induce vomiting, UN1268 class 3 PG II. sources.name: Klean-Strip safety data sheets (Denatured Alcohol, VM&P Naphtha, Kerosene)
sources.note: Denatured Alcohol rev 2023-08-10 (ethanol 30-90%, methanol 5-60%, flash 7 C / 45 F Setaflash, H301/H311/H331/H370, blindness, delayed symptoms 6-30 h, solid water streams spread fire). VM&P Naphtha rev 2015-12-30 (paint thinner use, flash 69 F TCC; https://www1.mscdirect.com/MSDS/MSDS00052/70250410-20160522.PDF). sources.name: Hess safety data sheets (Kerosene K1 and K2 No. 0290; Gasoline, All Grades)
sources.note: Both rev 2012-08-30. Gasoline: flash -45 F, benzene 0.1-4.9%, Carc/Muta 1B, use only as a motor fuel. Kerosene (https://monroetn.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Kerosene.pdf): CAS 8008-20-6, flash above 38 C, carcinogenicity Category 2, naphthalene 0.04%, autoignition 210 C (410 F), vapour travel, do not induce vomiting.

sources.name: ExxonMobil product specifications and safety data sheets (Isopar sales specifications; No. 2 Diesel SDS)
sources.note: Isopar minimum flash points from the sales specifications (not SDSs): G 40 C (eff. 2018-06-11), H 49 C (2020-09-07), L 62 C (2015-04-01), M 93.5 C (2014-07-01); G and L aromatics max 0.01 wt%. The spec sheets forbid redistribution, so facts only. No. 2 Diesel SDS rev 2019-10-22: flash above 38 C, H351, for use as a motor fuel only (https://www.exxon.com/-/media/project/wep/exxon/exxon-retail-us/us-fuel-delivery/pdf/no-2-diesel-fuel-safety-data-sheet.pdf).

sources.name: Firefly Paraffin Lamp Oil Safety Data Sheet
sources.note: Revised 2023-10-10. C12-15 branched and linear alkanes above 95%, flash 83.5 C (182.3 F) closed cup, Flam. Liq. 4, H304, explosive mixture possible when sprayed or atomised, static accumulator, do not induce vomiting.

sources.name: Lamplight Farms safety data sheets (Ultra Pure and Medallion Lamp Oil; TIKI Citronella and Clean Burn Torch Fuels)
sources.note: Ultra Pure MSDS rev 3, 2007-01-09: flash 97 C (207 F), autoignition above 200 C, vapour pressure below 0.01 mmHg, not DOT regulated; internally inconsistent on appearance and odour. The 2002 Ultra Pure MSDS (121 C / 250 F, autoignition 216 C, freezes 8 C / 47 F) is read as reproduced in the Kindle Arts guidelines. Medallion SDS Rev 05, 2015-05-11: hydrotreated light distillate, flash 63 C / 145 F (https://media.lifeandhome.com/media/downloads/29778/41786953_SDS.pdf). TIKI Citronella Torch Fuel Rev 03 2015: flash 62.8-135 C, autoignition above 220 C. TIKI Clean Burn rev 2015-07-30: coconut fatty acid methyl esters, flash above 93.9 C. Medallion and TIKI citronella carry no static precaution.

sources.name: North American Fire Arts Association Performer Safety Guidelines

sources.note: Nail Gun Safety: A Guide for Construction Contractors, with OSHA, DHHS (NIOSH) Publication No. 2011-202, OSHA Publication 3459-8-11, September 2011, which states it is in the public domain (read 2026-10-03 from https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/209984/cdc_209984_DS1.pdf; catalogue record https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/6013): about 37,000 emergency room visits a year; full sequential triggers safest and contact triggers twice the injury risk; hands at least 12 inches from the nailing point; disconnect the air to clear jams; never bypass safety features; ANSI Z87.1 eye protection and hearing protection; seek medical care at once. cdc.gov and stacks.cdc.gov refuse scripted downloads; the PDF was fetched through the web reader. The niosh-pocket-guide entry covers only the chemical hazards pocket guide. Also used from the nail gun guide (re-read 2026-10-03): always shoot away from your body and co-workers; never use the nailer with the non-dominant hand; disconnect the compressed air when leaving the gun, on ladders and stairs, passing it, clearing jams and in maintenance; scaffolds rather than ladders, sequential triggers on ladders, three points of contact; safety shoes. The guide covers air nailers only and says nothing about cordless ones.
